prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal]
First level of an original Win95-style archery game in `game/index.html`, single file, no build.

[action]
- Wrote "Balloon Bowman": canvas game with all sound synthesized in WebAudio; the only external request is the Silkscreen font from Google Fonts (falls back to monospace).
- Assumptions I made:
  - Aiming is slingshot style: press anywhere, drag back, release. Drag length sets power; a dotted arc previews the shot.
  - Balloons rise on the right. Pop 30 to clear the level; 3 escaping off the top is game over.
  - One arrow can pierce several balloons for a combo multiplier; small fast gold balloons score 50.
  - Click (or Space/Enter) starts and restarts; best score is kept in localStorage.
- Feel: bow creak ticks rising in pitch as you draw, twang and whoosh on release, pop pitch climbing with combo and streak, hit-stop, screen shake, confetti, score popups, thud when an arrow sticks in the ground.

[result]
- Headless logic smoke test (node, stubbed DOM, simulated pointer events), output:
```
start {"state":"play","score":0,"lives":3,"popped":0,"shots":0,"nb":0}
after shooting {"state":"play","score":10,"lives":3,"popped":1,"shots":8,"nb":2}
idle run {"state":"over","score":10,"lives":0,"popped":1,"shots":8,"nb":0}
```
  This shows start, shooting, a hit scoring, and the lose path all work.
- Render check hook: "0 console errors"; the screenshot shows the title panel, HUD, archer and scene drawing correctly with the font loaded.
- Not verified: I did not play it by hand in a browser, so the sound and the difficulty tuning are unheard and untested by feel. The level-clear screen was not reached in the test.
- I opened no browser tabs or apps, so there is nothing to close. The test script is in `tmp/smoke.js`.

[next]
Open `game/index.html` and play a minute; the likely tuning knobs are spawn rate and balloon speed in `spawnBalloon` and `update`.
